title: Quería que vinieras: the sequence of tenses
summary: The main verb picks the subjunctive: quiero que vengas, but quería que vinieras. It also covers como si, para que in the past and me gustaría que.
focus: Matching the subjunctive to the tense of the main verb
content:
## The main verb sets the tense

After **que**, the tense of the main verb picks the subjunctive (forms recap: **vinieron → viniera**).

| Main verb | Subjunctive | Example |
|---|---|---|
| present | present | **Quiero que vengas.** (I want you to come.) |
| present perfect | present | **Me ha pedido que lo haga.** (She's asked me to do it.) |
| future | present | **Te pediré que me ayudes.** (I'll ask you to help me.) |
| preterite | imperfect | **Me pidió que lo hiciera.** (She asked me to do it.) |
| imperfect | imperfect | **Quería que vinieras.** (I wanted you to come.) |
| conditional | imperfect | **Me gustaría que fueras.** (I'd like you to go.) |

Now or later takes the present subjunctive; past or conditional takes the imperfect.

## Wanting, asking and needing in the past

Every trigger of the subjunctive works in the past: move both verbs back.

- **Mis padres querían que estudiara medicina.** (My parents wanted me to study medicine.)
- **El médico me aconsejó que caminara más.** (The doctor advised me to walk more.)
- **Era necesario que alguien hablara con la directora.** (Someone had to talk to the head teacher.)
- **Era importante que no llegáramos tarde.** (It was important that we weren't late.)
- **No hacía falta que trajeras vino.** (You didn't need to bring wine.)

With no particular person, the impersonal phrases take an infinitive: **era necesario esperar** (it was necessary to wait). Name a person and you need **que + subjunctive**.

## Para que in the past

**Para que** (so that) always takes the subjunctive, and it follows the main verb like any other trigger:

- **Te lo digo para que lo sepas.** (I'm telling you so that you know.)
- **Te lo dije para que lo supieras.** (I told you so that you'd know.)
- **Mi abuelo trabajó mucho para que sus hijos pudieran estudiar.** (My grandfather worked hard so that his children could study.)

When both verbs share the same subject, use **para + infinitive** instead: **Ahorré para comprarme un coche** (I saved to buy myself a car), but **Ahorré para que mi hija se comprara un coche** (I saved so that my daughter could buy herself a car).

## Me gustaría que: polite wishes

A conditional main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive even when the wish is about now or tomorrow. It is the polite way to ask for something:

- **Me gustaría que vinieras mañana.** (I'd like you to come tomorrow.)
- **Preferiría que no fumaras aquí.** (I'd rather you didn't smoke here.)
- **Sería mejor que se lo dijeras tú.** (It would be better if you told him.)

Compare **Me gusta que vengas** (I like it when you come) with **Me gustaría que vinieras** (I'd like you to come). In parts of Latin America you will hear *me gustaría que vengas* in casual speech; in standard Spanish, keep the imperfect.

## Como si: as if

**Como si** (as if) always takes the imperfect subjunctive, whatever the tense of the main verb, because it compares with something that is not real:

- **Habla como si fuera el jefe.** (He talks as if he were the boss.)
- **Me miró como si no me conociera.** (She looked at me as if she didn't know me.)
- **Gasta como si tuviera un millón de euros.** (He spends as if he had a million euros.)
- **Hice como si no pasara nada.** (I acted as if nothing were going on.)

Never put the present subjunctive after **como si**. Say **como si fuera**, not *como si sea*.

vocabulary.meaning: to beg, to ask earnestly (+ que + subjunctive)
vocabulary.example: Le rogué que no se lo contara a nadie.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I begged him not to tell anyone.

vocabulary.example: El cliente exigió que le cambiaran la mesa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The customer demanded that they change his table.

vocabulary.example: Mi profesora me aconsejó que leyera más novelas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My teacher advised me to read more novels.

vocabulary.example: Mis padres no permitían que viéramos la tele entre semana.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My parents didn't allow us to watch TV on weekdays.

vocabulary.example: El médico le prohibió que comiera sal.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The doctor forbade him to eat salt.

vocabulary.example: Insistió en que nos quedáramos a cenar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: She insisted that we stay for dinner.

vocabulary.example: Te sugerí que lo dejaras para mañana.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I suggested you leave it until tomorrow.

vocabulary.meaning: to avoid, to prevent (evitar que = to stop something happening)
vocabulary.example: Cerré la ventana para evitar que entrara el frío.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I closed the window to stop the cold getting in.

vocabulary.meaning: to be needed (no hacía falta que = there was no need to)
vocabulary.example: No hacía falta que trajerais nada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: You didn't need to bring anything.

vocabulary.example: Habla como si lo supiera todo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He talks as if he knew everything.

vocabulary.example: Dejé la luz encendida para que el niño no tuviera miedo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I left the light on so that the boy wouldn't be scared.

vocabulary.meaning: it was necessary that (+ imperfect subjunctive)
vocabulary.example: Era necesario que alguien llamara al fontanero.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Someone needed to call the plumber.

vocabulary.meaning: it was important that (+ imperfect subjunctive)
vocabulary.example: Era importante que todos firmaran a tiempo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It was important that everyone signed on time.

vocabulary.example: Me gustaría que me llamaras más a menudo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'd like you to call me more often.

quiz.prompt: Mi médica me aconsejó que ___ más. (dormir)
quiz.explanation: Aconsejó is a preterite, so the subjunctive goes into the past: 'que durmiera' (from durmieron).
hints: A past main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Te ruego que me ___ la verdad. (decir)
quiz.explanation: Ruego is a present, so the present subjunctive follows: 'que me digas la verdad'.
hints: Is the main verb present or past?

quiz.prompt: Era importante que nosotros ___ a tiempo. (llegar)
quiz.explanation: Era importante is in the past, so 'que llegáramos' (accent on the nosotros form). The -se form llegásemos is also correct.

quiz.prompt: Me miró como si no me ___. (conocer)
quiz.explanation: Como si always takes the imperfect subjunctive: 'como si no me conociera'.
hints: Como si never takes the present subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Dejé la llave debajo del felpudo para que tú ___ entrar. (poder)
quiz.explanation: Dejé is past, so para que takes the imperfect subjunctive: 'para que pudieras' (from pudieron).
hints: Para que follows the main verb's tense.

quiz.prompt: Me gustaría que ___ conmigo al concierto. (venir, tú)
quiz.explanation: A conditional main verb (me gustaría) takes the imperfect subjunctive, even for a future plan: 'que vinieras'.
hints: Me gustaría que takes the imperfect subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: El cliente exigió que le ___ el dinero. (devolver, ellos)
quiz.explanation: Exigió is a preterite: 'que le devolvieran el dinero' (from devolvieron).
hints: A preterite main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Si me llama mañana, le aconsejaré que ___ con su jefe. (hablar)
quiz.explanation: Aconsejaré is a future, and a future main verb takes the present subjunctive: 'que hable con su jefe'.
hints: A future main verb takes the present subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: No hacía falta que vosotros ___ tan pronto. (venir)
quiz.explanation: Hacía is an imperfect, so 'que vinierais' (from vinieron).

quiz.prompt: Mis padres no permitían que mi hermana y yo ___ solos a la playa. (ir)
quiz.explanation: Permitían is an imperfect, so the imperfect subjunctive follows: 'que fuéramos' (ir: fueron → fuéramos).

conversations.title: The new boss
conversations.scenario: Lucía tells her brother Javier about her first week at a new job.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Qué tal tu primera semana en el trabajo?
lines.meaning: How was your first week at work?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Rara. El primer día mi jefa me pidió que llegara a las siete.
lines.meaning: Strange. On the first day my boss asked me to arrive at seven.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿A las siete? ¿Era necesario que estuvieras allí tan pronto?
lines.meaning: At seven? Did you really need to be there so early?
lines.note: era necesario que takes the imperfect subjunctive

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Según ella, sí. Quería que conociera a todo el equipo antes de la reunión.
lines.meaning: According to her, yes. She wanted me to meet the whole team before the meeting.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Lo haría para que te sintieras parte del grupo, ¿no?
lines.meaning: She probably did it so that you'd feel part of the group, right?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Puede ser. Pero luego me habló como si llevara diez años allí.
lines.meaning: Maybe. But then she spoke to me as if I'd been there for ten years.
lines.note: como si takes the imperfect subjunctive

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Hice como si lo entendiera todo, claro.
lines.meaning: I acted as if I understood everything, of course.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Me gustaría que me la presentaras algún día.
lines.meaning: I'd like you to introduce her to me some day.
lines.note: me gustaría que takes the imperfect subjunctive

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Ni hablar! Prefiero que no os conozcáis.
lines.meaning: No way! I'd rather you two didn't meet.
lines.note: A present main verb takes the present subjunctive.

listening.meaning: I wanted you to listen to me.
listening.note: An imperfect main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive.

listening.text: Le pedí que cerrara la puerta.
listening.meaning: I asked him to close the door.

listening.text: Hablaba como si estuviera muy cansado.
listening.meaning: He was talking as if he were very tired.
listening.note: Como si takes the imperfect subjunctive.

listening.text: Era necesario que todos firmaran el contrato.
listening.meaning: Everyone had to sign the contract.

listening.text: Me gustaría que pasáramos más tiempo juntos.
listening.meaning: I'd like us to spend more time together.

listening.text: Mi abuela nos daba dinero para que compráramos helados.
listening.meaning: My grandmother used to give us money so that we could buy ice creams.

listening.text: El entrenador insistió en que bebiéramos agua durante el partido.
listening.meaning: The coach insisted that we drink water during the match.
listening.note: New word: el entrenador = the coach.

listening.text: Nos prohibieron que hiciéramos fotos dentro del museo, pero nadie hizo caso.
listening.meaning: They forbade us to take photos inside the museum, but nobody paid attention.
listening.note: New word: hacer caso = to pay attention.

guide.section: The main verb sets the tense

guide.tip: Ask one question. Does the main verb point at now or later (present subjunctive), or at the past or a would-be (imperfect subjunctive)?

bites.title: The tenses agree
bites.rule: A main verb in the present, perfect or future takes the present subjunctive. A main verb in the preterite, imperfect or conditional takes the imperfect subjunctive.
bites.example: Quiero que vengas. Quería que vinieras.
bites.example_meaning: I want you to come. I wanted you to come.

bites.title: Para que goes back too
bites.rule: Para que follows the main verb: lo hago para que lo sepas, lo hice para que lo supieras. Same subject in both? Use para + infinitive.
bites.example: Te lo dije para que lo supieras.
bites.example_meaning: I told you so that you'd know.

bites.title: Me gustaría que…
bites.rule: A conditional main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive, even for tomorrow: me gustaría que vinieras mañana.
bites.example: Me gustaría que me ayudaras con la mudanza.
bites.example_meaning: I'd like you to help me with the move.

bites.title: Como si = as if
bites.rule: Como si always takes the imperfect subjunctive, whatever the tense of the main verb: habla como si fuera el jefe.
bites.example: Me miró como si no me conociera.
bites.example_meaning: She looked at me as if she didn't know me.

sorts.title: Which subjunctive follows?
sorts.why: Present, perfect and future main verbs take the present subjunctive; preterite, imperfect and conditional ones take the imperfect.

sorts.title: Infinitive or que?
sorts.why: Same subject in both halves takes para + infinitive; a different subject takes para que + subjunctive.

items.text: Te di dinero ___ te compraras una moto.
Me levanté pronto ___ no llegar tarde.
Desperté a mi hermano ___ no llegara tarde.

spots.sentence: Quería que vengas a mi fiesta.
spots.why: Quería is past, so the imperfect subjunctive follows.

spots.sentence: Me gustaría que me ayudes con la mudanza.
spots.why: Me gustaría que takes the imperfect subjunctive in standard Spanish.

spots.sentence: Habla como si sea el dueño de la casa.
spots.why: Como si always takes the imperfect subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Te lo expliqué para que lo entiendas.
spots.why: Expliqué is past, so para que takes the imperfect subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Era necesario que todos estén presentes.
spots.why: Era necesario is past, so the imperfect subjunctive follows.

spots.sentence: Te pido que me llamaras esta noche.
spots.why: Pido is present, so the present subjunctive follows.

builds.text: Quería que vinieras a mi boda.
builds.meaning: I wanted you to come to my wedding.

builds.text: Me gustaría que me escribieras más.
builds.meaning: I'd like you to write to me more.

builds.text: Lo dije para que lo supieras.
builds.meaning: I said it so that you'd know.

builds.text: Me miraba como si no me conociera.
builds.meaning: He was looking at me as if he didn't know me.

builds.text: Era importante que lo hiciéramos juntos.
builds.meaning: It was important that we did it together.
